feature: Start a UI design from an empty window
summary: An empty window now offers Design UI. One click opens untitled-ui: a 1280 x 800 canvas holding a Login screen laid out as a column, with the Library already on Components, so the next thing you do is drag a Button onto it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open a new window with nothing in it (Shift Command N). Walk: design-ui-start-walk.

try.do: In a new empty window, click Design UI, the last row of the card.
Look at what opened: the Login screen in the middle of the canvas, Layers showing Login, the Library open on Comps.
Click the Login screen and resize it by a corner handle, then press Command Z.
Drag the Button tile from the Library onto the bottom of the Login screen.
Press Command Z twice: the Button goes, the Login screen stays.
With that window in front, choose File > New UI Design: a second window, untitled-ui 2, opens.

evaluate: Is Design UI the row you would look for when you want to build a screen, or would you have tried Blank canvas first?
Does the Button landing as a full-width bar at the bottom of the column feel like it went where you dropped it?
Is a Login screen the right thing to start with, or would you rather start from an empty column of the same size?
Should File > New UI Design have a shortcut, given every Command N is already taken?
rough: The mock's front door (a window with a prompt bar, four template tiles and Recent, where Design UI turns the main button into New UI canvas) is not built; this is one row of today's empty card. Filed as new-window-opens-a-front-door-with-a-starting-te.

The tool bar is the full set, not the mock's UI strip of Select, Frame, Component, Shape, Pen, Text, Measure, Hand and Zoom; the window opens in Everything. Covered by new-window-opens-a-front-door-with-a-starting-te, where the template sets the Design mode.

Layers lists Login's rows bottom first (top of the stack first, as everywhere in the app), where the mock lists them in reading order. Decision card on a-column-lists-its-rows-in-the-order-the-user-ch.

The dropped Button reads Button, and its Properties show a Label row and no Variant row; the mock's step 7 shows Button · Primary with Variant Primary and Label Sign in. Covered by an-instance-s-properties-match-the-variants-mock.
The Login screen closes around its rows and grows when the Button lands, which matches the mock's drawing of it.

The title bar shows the mode chip and no name, the shell every still picture already has; the 1280 x 800 reads in Layers as Canvas. The window is named untitled-ui, which the Window menu and a walk both read.
